1.title: Testing Applications
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Testing Applications. It covers the exam area Domain three: Testing and Deployment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Develop and validate tests with A W S S A M, A W S C D K and A W S Cloud Formation (three point two.one). Use mock A P Is for external dependencies (three point two.two). Create application test events (three point two.three). Create and configure application environments (three point two.four). Use A W S A I tools to generate tests and automate repetitive testing (three point two.five). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain three: Testing and Deployment (twenty-two percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: Tests you write and run
1.text: Tests you write and run. Unit test. One function or module with no network; use mocks for A W S calls. Integration test. Components working together (for example Lambda plus Dynamo D B) in a test environment. End-to-end test. A full flow through the deployed system. Regression test. Old behavior still works after a change.

1.title: Tests you write and run, continued
1.text: Tests you write and run. The figure shows this: A test pyramid: many unit tests, fewer integration tests, few end-to-end tests.

1.title: AWS SAM, CDK and CloudFormation for testing
1.text: A W S S A M, C D K and Cloud Formation for testing. A W S S A M C L I. sam local invoke runs a Lambda function locally in a container with a test event; sam local start api runs an A P I locally. A W S C D K. Define infrastructure in code, so you can unit-test the generated templates and create test stacks. A W S Cloud Formation. Validate templates; create disposable test stacks from the same template as production. Exam tip: "Test a Lambda function on my laptop with an event" equals S A M local invoke.

1.title: Test events and mock dependencies
1.text: Test events and mock dependencies. Test events. Jason payloads that look like real events (an A P I Gateway request, an S three notification, an S Q S message) used to invoke a function (console test events, sam local invoke the event flag ). A P I Gateway test invoke. Send a test request to a method without a client. Mock integration. A P I Gateway returns a fixed response with no backend, so front-end teams can work before the backend exists. Mocks and stubs in code. Replace A W S S D K calls in unit tests so tests are fast and free.

1.title: Environments
1.text: Environments. Lambda versions and aliases. Alias dev, test, prod point to versions. A P I Gateway stages. One A P I, several stages. Container image tags. dev, prod or version tags in E C R. A W S Amplify branches. A Git branch gets its own hosted environment. A W S Copilot environments. Environments for containerized apps. Separate stacks or accounts. Strongest isolation.

1.title: AI tools for testing
1.text: A I tools for testing. A W S A I tools can generate test cases, run tests automatically, analyze results, support regression testing and suggest coverage gaps. As with all A I output, the developer reviews generated tests: a test that always passes proves nothing. Exam tip: A I-generated tests are a starting point. Check that they assert real behavior and cover edge cases. Exam tip: Unit tests use mocks; integration tests use a real test environment. If the question says no network, it is a unit test.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A developer wants to run a Lambda function locally with a sample S three event before deploying. Which tool fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A W S S A M C L I sam local invoke. S A M local runs the function in a local container with a test event.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Front-end developers need an A P I to call before the backend exists. What can the back-end team set up in A P I Gateway? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A mock integration. A mock integration returns a fixed response with no backend.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A unit test of a function that writes to Dynamo D B must not call A W S. What should the test use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A mock or stub of the S D K call. Mocks keep unit tests fast, free and isolated.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants dev, test and prod versions of one Lambda function. What should they use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Versions and aliases. Aliases point to immutable versions for each environment.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What is the best description of a test event? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A Jason payload shaped like a real event used to invoke a function. Test events imitate real triggers.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team uses an A I tool that writes unit tests. What should the developer do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Review the tests for real assertions and edge cases. Generated tests need human review.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does sam local invoke do? Answer: Runs a Lambda function locally with a test event. Question two. What is a mock integration? Answer: An A P I Gateway method that returns a fixed response with no backend. Question three. What is a Lambda alias? Answer: A named pointer to a function version.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Name two environment mechanisms. Answer: For example A P I Gateway stages and Lambda aliases. Question five. What does a unit test avoid? Answer: Network calls and real A W S resources, by using mocks. Question six. Who checks A I-generated tests? Answer: The developer.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Test types: unit (mocks), integration, end-to-end, regression. Local: S A M local invoke and start-api. Events and mocks: Jason test events, A P I Gateway mock integration, S D K mocks. Environments: aliases, stages, image tags, Amplify branches, Copilot environments. A I tools: generate and automate tests; review the output. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
